 8th Pay Commission Lists Five Key Website Updates
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 14, 2026
 # 8th Pay Commission 
 # Central Government Employees 
 # Pensioners 
 # Pay Revision 
 # Salary Hike 
 # Fitment Factor 
 # Stakeholder Consultations 
 # Government Employees 
 # Pension Revision 
 # 8th CPC 
 Recent notices cover stakeholder consultations and administrative changes, but offer no confirmation on salary hikes, fitment factor or pension revisions
  The Eighth Central Pay Commission has listed five key developments on its official website, covering stakeholder consultations across cities and changes to its consultant engagement guidelines. The updates provide an indication of the commission's ongoing administrative and consultation work, but do not announce any decision on revised salaries, pensions or the fitment factor.
 The latest notice, dated 21 September 2026, concerned the commission's visit to Mumbai on 22 and 23 October, with applications for stakeholder interactions closing on 10 October. Earlier notices included consultations in Bengaluru on 7 and 8 October, Jaipur on 31 August and 1 September, and Chandigarh from 16 to 18 September.
 Another update, issued on 11 August, announced a partial modification to the guidelines for engaging consultants. These developments form part of the commission's wider exercise of gathering inputs from employee associations, pensioners, unions and other stakeholders before preparing its recommendations.
 The commission has also conducted consultations in several other cities, including Delhi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata and Lucknow. Its memorandum submission process closed on 15 June 2026, while responses to an 18-question questionnaire hosted on the MyGov portal closed on 31 March.
 Constituted on 3 November 2025 under the chairpersonship of Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, the three-member commission has been given 18 months to submit its recommendations, placing the broad deadline around May 2027. It can also submit interim reports on specific matters.
 For central government employees and pensioners, the key issues remain the fitment factor, revised basic pay, allowances and pension adjustments. However, none of the five website updates confirms a salary increase, a revised pay matrix or an implementation date. These decisions will depend on the commission's final recommendations and the Union government's subsequent approval.
